verdict_reason: All three kernels are exact and the two blockers from my round-4 verdict are closed. (a) The RAW branch now has the magnitude guard it lacked: on the 3x2 input with a = 2.800000032174e38, `schatten_1` returns 4.849742563662358e+38 against the exact a*sqrt(3) = 4.849742316919859e+38 (rel 5.09e-08) where it previously returned a silently finite 0.0. (b) `_rankme.__defaults__` is now the RELEASED (1e-07,), not BLME's 1e-12, and it is Garrido Eq. 2's ratio-plus-epsilon form: on I_2 it gives 1.999999877258836 at every one of the seven contract scales from 1e-30 to 1e20. Head-to-head against the released MLGroupJLU/MatrixNuclearNorm `code/MNN.py`, `_normalise_matrix` is `torch.equal` BIT-IDENTICAL to the official `normalize()` on 100/100 ordinary random matrices (max abs diff 0.0) and `row_normalized_matrix_nuclear_norm` equals `matrix_nuclear_norm(normalize(R))/T` at exactly 0.000e+00 relative error on 60 synthetic matrices and again at 0.000e+00 on real pythia-70m and pythia-160m states over 100 WikiText passages. Analytic anchors on I_2: schatten_1 = 2.000000000 exactly, schatten_4 = 1.189207115002721 = 2^(1/4) exactly, MNN/T = 0.9999999404. Round-3's two extreme counterexamples are both repaired: rows of +/-7.000000233745e17 * ones(768) give MNN/T = 0.0510310344 against the analytic 0.0510310363 (3.7e-08), and the 2.8e38 centring case returns 0.5773502588 against sqrt(3)/3 = 0.5773502692 (1.8e-08). Over a 128x256 cloud swept from 1e-30 to 1e35, schatten_1/s is constant to 1.3e-07 relative, rankme to 3e-08 and MNN/T exactly.
comparable_reason: The two PROMOTED keys are not gauge-invariant, which is a stronger objection than a correlation. gpt2's final LayerNorm removes the scale of its input, so multiplying the deepest block's output by 8 leaves the logits unchanged to 3.643e-07 RELATIVE (max absolute delta 1.221e-04 on a 50257-wide logit tensor) -- yet `schatten_1` moves 13575.912249 -> 108607.297993 and `schatten_4` 3977.768408 -> 31822.147267, both by exactly 8.000000000. A function-preserving reparameterisation can therefore set these two features to any value. In the same test `rankme` (17.806460007), `row_normalized_matrix_nuclear_norm` (0.5761633391) and `row_normalized_schatten_inf` (8.1022844315) are exactly invariant, so those three are the usable members of the family. Separately, MNN is basis-dependent by construction (it sums the top-D COLUMN L2 norms): rotating one real gpt2 block by a random orthogonal 768x768 moves MNN/T 0.426403701 -> 0.621885002, so it is not an isometry invariant either. On the 65-model archive: rho(d_model) = -0.952 for row_normalized_schatten_1_last, -0.716 for _4, +0.113 for _inf, -0.133 for MNN/T, +0.377 for rankme; on a fresh 5-model panel (distilgpt2, gpt2, pythia-70m, pythia-160m, gpt2-medium) schatten_1_last spans 1468.6 to 26536.5 with rho(d_model) = +0.894.
normalized_variant: _meta_row_normalized_schatten_1, _meta_row_normalized_schatten_4 (the manuscript's ||H||_p / d_model^{1/p} form, both demoted to _meta_)
github_reason: I fetched `code/MNN.py` from the released repo (master branch) and executed its `normalize()` and `matrix_nuclear_norm()` verbatim, together with the driver's `mnn / len(token_ids[0])` normalisation. `_normalise_matrix` is `torch.equal` True against `normalize` on 100/100 ordinary random matrices (T in 8..200, D in 16..800, magnitudes 0.1x to 50x), and MNN/T agrees at exactly 0.000e+00 relative on 60 further matrices and on real pythia-70m/160m `last_hidden_state` tensors over 100 WikiText-103 passages. The conditional-guard design is confirmed by construction as well as by measurement: for float32 at D = 768 the safe band is [4.3368e-19, 1.6641e+17], so the rescale never fires on real activations and bit-equality with the reference is preserved. The prompt's second stated property does NOT hold -- the rescale is by the actual maximum (`X / _gmax`, `X / _rmax`, `_Zr = Z / _rmax_r`), not by a power of two -- but the measured consequence is smaller than the alternative: at a = 2.8e38 the shipped form gives rel 5.09e-08 against the exact value, while a 2^floor(log2 max) rescale gives 9.56e-08, because the float32 SVD dominates the error. Yusupov et al. (Schatten) and Garrido et al. (RankMe) released no runnable LLM pipeline; RankMe Eq. 2 is short enough that I implemented it directly and the shipped `_rankme` matches it.
paper_reason: Li et al. arXiv:2410.10672 Table 11 (Wikipedia row) publishes Matrix Nuclear-Norm for the Pythia family: 0.6996 (70M), 0.6718 (160M), 0.6464 (410M). This anchor DOES exist -- my own round-4 verdict said I could not find it and was wrong; it is Table 11, not Table 10, and Table 10 is the Cerebras-GPT set. Running BLME's MNN kernel on the released extraction route over 100 WikiText-103 validation passages (mean 131.9 tokens) gives 0.604393 for pythia-70m (-13.61%) and 0.514485 for pythia-160m (-23.42%), with the published ORDERING (70m above 160m) reproduced. The kernel is not the source of the gap -- it is bit-exact (0.000e+00) against the released code on those same tensors -- the corpus is: Li et al. use 10,000 randomly sampled Pile-Wikipedia entries truncated at 2048 tokens, and MNN is strongly length-dependent (their own Table 13 shows it rising from 0.4574 at length 64 to 0.9132 at 1024 for Cerebras-GPT-111M). Yusupov et al. publish only figure axes (1e3-1e4) for MLP-internal Schatten norms; Garrido et al. report RankMe for SSL vision encoders. The exact analytic anchors are reproduced instead: on I_2, schatten_1 = 2.000000000 and schatten_4 = 2^(1/4) = 1.189207115002721 with zero error.
confounds_reason: For the promoted keys the confound is mechanical, not statistical: `schatten_1` and `schatten_4` are homogeneous of degree 1 in the representation scale, and the representation scale of the last block is a free gauge parameter under the final LayerNorm (8x rescale, logits unchanged to 3.6e-07, features x8.0 exactly). Their cross-model variation is therefore activation magnitude first and geometry second; on the 5-model panel rho(d_model) = +0.894, rho(n_layers) = +0.738. For the demoted d-divided keys the confound is manufactured by the divisor: a zero-padding isometry 768 -> 1536 -> 3072 leaves schatten_1 at ratios 1.000000011 / 0.999999829 and rankme bit-identical (12.275810) while _meta_row_normalized_schatten_1 falls to exactly 0.499999984 / 0.249999996 and _meta_row_normalized_schatten_4 to 0.840896496 / 0.707106623 (= 2^-1/4, 4^-1/4). On 65 archived models that reads as rho(d_model) = -0.952. rankme and MNN/T are the two keys with no mechanical width term.
defects: PAPER (not code): sections/metrics_geometry.tex:296-304 defines the reported quantity as ||H||_p / d_model^{1/p} and appendix_normalization.tex:20 tabulates that divisor, but the manuscript's own Eq. (schatten-scaling) shows the residual dimension factor is d^{1/p - 1/2}, not d^{1/p}. Dividing by d^{1/p} therefore OVER-corrects by d^{-1/2}, and when N < d_model (the shipped case: 128 tokens, 768-4096 dims) r = min(N,d) = N so the norm has no d_model dependence at all and the whole divisor is artifact. Numerically, at N=128, d=4096, p=1 a flat spectrum gives ||H||_1 = 128.000000 exactly regardless of d, which the paper's divisor turns into 3.125000e-02. The code is right to demote these keys; the manuscript must be reconciled.

DOC/CODE CONTRADICTION, schatten.py:36-41 vs 254-279: the module docstring still says 'BLME centres columns then row-L2-normalises ... Treat `schatten_*` as BLME's row-normalized variant', while the return dict two hundred lines later says 'Paper form: RAW matrix, no divisor' and the code computes `schatten_1`/`schatten_4`/`rankme` from `S_raw = svdvals(Z)` on the unpreprocessed matrix. The class docstring at 372-386 also advertises `row_normalized_schatten_1_last`/`_4_last` as reported keys although both are now `_meta_`-prefixed, and says MNN is 'normalised by d' when it is normalised by T. Three stale statements about which quantity is shipped.

CODE/INTEGRATION, core.py:215-249 vs schatten.py:392-396: `geometry_schatten` is NOT in `cache_hidden_tasks`, yet `use_cache` defaults to True and `_collect_per_layer` consumes any populated shared cache. The cache tokenises at a hard-coded 512 (cache.py:422) while defaults.yaml pins this task at max_length 128, so the emitted values depend on which OTHER tasks happened to co-run. This is the same class as the `geometry_isoscore` co-runner bug fixed in round 4 and it has not been fixed here.

PROTOCOL/ATTRIBUTION: Yusupov et al. Eq. 5 is the Schatten norm of MLP-internal activations averaged over layers; BLME reports the deepest residual-stream BLOCK output. The module docstring states this divergence in its first half and contradicts it in its second, so a reader cannot tell which is meant.

GUARD PROPERTY: the conditional rescale is by the actual maximum, not by a power of two, so it is exact only to float32 SVD precision when it fires (rel 5.09e-08 at 2.8e38). Bit-equality on ordinary data is preserved because the guard does not fire there (safe band [4.3368e-19, 1.6641e+17] at D=768), so this costs nothing measurable -- but the code comment's claim that the rescale 'only shifts exponents' is false as written.

COMPARABILITY: `schatten_1`/`schatten_4` are gauge-dependent (x8.0 under a rescale that leaves the logits identical to 3.6e-07), and MNN is basis-dependent (0.426403701 -> 0.621885002 under a random orthogonal rotation). Neither belongs in a cross-model feature matrix without an explicit activation-scale control.
fix: No kernel change. 1) Rewrite the module and class docstrings so that all three statements agree with the code: `schatten_1`/`schatten_4`/`rankme` are computed on the RAW deepest-block matrix with no centring, no row-L2 and no divisor; `row_normalized_*` are the centred + row-L2 forms; MNN is normalised by T, not d; the `_meta_`-prefixed keys are not reported. 2) Reconcile sections/metrics_geometry.tex:296-304 and appendix_normalization.tex:20 to the demotion, quoting the corrected exponent d^{1/p-1/2} and the measured 0.25x zero-padding factor. 3) Set `use_cache: false` for geometry_schatten in defaults.yaml, or register it in core.py's cache_hidden_tasks, so its 128-token window is not silently replaced by the cache's 512. 4) Optionally emit an activation-scale-normalised companion (e.g. schatten_1 / ||H||_F) so a gauge-invariant nuclear-norm feature exists alongside the raw one.
